children: The Tata Trusts Chairman will step down from leadership roles at Trent, Voltas, Tata Investment Corporation, Tata International, Tata Steel and Titan Company on 12 November 2026, in line with the group’s retirement policy

Noel Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, is set to step down from the boards of six Tata Group companies on 12 November 2026, when he turns 70. The planned exits align with the group’s corporate governance framework, which sets a retirement age of 70 for non-executive, non-independent directors and 65 for executive directors.

The transition will affect his positions as Non-Executive Chairman of Trent, Voltas, Tata Investment Corporation and Tata International, as well as Non-Executive Vice-Chairman of Tata Steel and Titan Company. Successor appointments for the affected leadership positions are expected to be finalised by the respective company boards ahead of the deadline.
Tata Sons & Other Board Positions To Continue

Despite stepping down from these operating company boards, Noel Tata is expected to retain his position as a Tata Trusts nominee director on the board of Tata Sons, the group’s principal holding company. Tata Trusts holds a controlling 66% equity stake in Tata Sons.

He will also remain on the board of Trent Hypermarket, the retail joint venture with Tesco that operates Star Bazaar stores, and continue as chairman of Dubai-based subsidiary Tata International West Asia DMCC.
The planned exits follow signals given at the annual general meetings of Trent and Voltas in June 2026, when Tata indicated that he would be serving his final terms as chairman.

The board changes come amid reported strategic differences between Noel Tata and Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran. Industry observers have pointed to internal deliberations concerning leadership succession, the interpretation of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association and potential regulatory routes for a public listing of the group’s principal holding company.
The upcoming changes mark a transition in leadership across six major Tata Group businesses, while Noel Tata is expected to retain his role at Tata Trusts and his position on the Tata Sons board.
